name: Jogging
setup: Players line up to jog around the field at a comfortable pace.
instructions: Players gently jog around the field to increase heart rate and warm up muscles. Allow gradual increase in intensity.
coaching_points: Comfortable pace, steady increase in tempo.

name: High Knees
setup: Players line up across the field.
instructions: While moving forward, players lift their knees as high as possible, alternating legs with each step.
coaching_points: Maintain upright posture; use arms to maintain balance and momentum.

name: Butt Kickers
setup: Players line up across the field.
instructions: Players kick their heels up toward their buttocks while moving forward, aiming for quick light contact.
coaching_points: Warms up quadriceps; improves leg turnover.

name: Side Shuffles
setup: Players line up sideways across the field.
instructions: Players move laterally with feet wide apart, shifting from side to side without crossing legs.
coaching_points: Activates lateral leg muscles; improves agility.

name: Arm Circles
setup: Players stand with arms extended parallel to the ground.
instructions: Make small to large circles, first forward, then reverse to backward direction.
coaching_points: Warms up shoulders, chest, upper back; preps upper body for throwing and batting.

name: Walking Lunges
setup: Players line up to walk forward.
instructions: Step forward into a lunge keeping front knee above the ankle (not past the toes). Alternate legs moving forward with each lunge.
coaching_points: Engages glutes, hamstrings, quads.

name: Inchworms
setup: Players start in a standing position.
instructions: Hinge at the waist, place hands on the ground, walk hands forward into plank position. Then walk feet toward the hands keeping legs straight. Repeat moving forward.
coaching_points: Full-body warmup; emphasize keeping legs straight on the foot-walk.

name: Carioca
setup: Players line up sideways across the field.
instructions: Move laterally, crossing trail leg in front of and then behind the lead leg, alternating.
coaching_points: Fluid, rhythmic; arms help balance. Improves footwork, hip flexibility, dynamic balance.

name: Leg Swings
setup: Players hold onto a fence or partner.
instructions: Swing one leg forward and backward, then switch legs. Can also be done side to side.
coaching_points: Warms up leg muscles and hip flexors; improves flexibility and ROM.

name: Spiderman Stretch
setup: Players start in a push-up position.
instructions: Step forward with one foot placing it outside the hand on the same side; bring hips down toward the ground to deepen the stretch. Hold briefly, return, repeat with the other leg.
coaching_points: Targets hip flexors, hamstrings, groin.

name: Forward Leg Swings
setup: Players find a stable object to hold.
instructions: Holding the object, swing one leg forward and backward in a controlled motion. Repeat with the other leg.
coaching_points: Warms up hip flexors, hamstrings, glutes; improves leg motion range.

name: Lateral Leg Swings
setup: Players find a stable object to hold.
instructions: Swing one leg side to side across the body in a controlled motion. Repeat with the other leg.
coaching_points: Targets adductors and abductors; promotes flexibility and hip coordination.

name: Skipping for Height
setup: Players line up to skip across the field.
instructions: Players skip forward, focusing on driving the knee up and exploding upward off the opposite leg to gain height. Land softly and continue skipping.
coaching_points: Ballistic warmup; improves coordination, lower body explosiveness, body awareness.

name: Dynamic Chest Stretch
setup: Players stand with arms extended in front of them.
instructions: Players swing their arms wide to the sides and back across the body in a hugging motion, returning to start.
coaching_points: Warms up chest, shoulders, upper back; preps upper body for throwing.

name: Arm Crosses
setup: Players stand with arms extended out to the sides.
instructions: Swing arms across the chest in a crossing motion (like a hug), then back out to a wide T position. Repeat fluidly.
coaching_points: Loosens shoulders and upper back.

name: Hip Circles
setup: Players stand with hands on hips and feet shoulder-width apart.
instructions: Standing on one foot, players make circles with the opposite knee in one direction, then the other. Repeat with the other leg.
coaching_points: Improves hip flexibility and mobility.

name: Backpedal to Sprint
setup: Players line up at one end of the field.
instructions: Players backpedal for a designated distance, then quickly transition to sprint forward for the same distance.
coaching_points: Trains transition between movement directions; key for fielding and base running.

name: Pinwheels
setup: Players stand with arms extended straight out at shoulder height.
instructions: Players rotate arms in opposite directions (one forward, one backward) for 10-15 seconds, then switch.
coaching_points: Improves shoulder coordination, mobility, and warms up rotator cuffs.

name: Frankensteins
setup: Players line up to walk forward.
instructions: Walking forward, players keep one leg straight and kick it up to the opposite hand. Alternate legs every step.
coaching_points: Warms up hamstrings; improves dynamic flexibility.

name: One Knee Dart Throw
setup: Players pair off about 5 feet apart on the ground. Glove-side knee up, throwing-side knee down on the ground.
instructions: Form a 'dart' with the throwing arm bent at 90 degrees, hand by ear. Throw the ball back and forth focusing on grip and a strong wrist snap. The ball is released from the partner so it arrives at the partner's chest.
coaching_points: Focus on grip, wrist snap, and a high release point. Don't bend forward.

name: One Knee Follow Through
setup: Players pair off about 10 feet apart. Glove-side knee up, throwing-side knee down.
instructions: Maintain the one-knee position used in the Dart Throw. Now players add a full follow-through, throwing the ball so the throwing hand finishes by the opposite hip.
coaching_points: Emphasize rotating the upper body while keeping the throwing-side knee down. Follow through across the body.

name: Standing Twist
setup: Players stand up and pair off about 15-20 feet apart.
instructions: Add a torso turn between throws. Players turn torso (load) before delivering each throw, then follow through.
coaching_points: Trains hip and shoulder separation; ball flight should improve as they engage their core.

name: Standing Throw from Stretch
setup: Players stand 20-30 feet apart in their throwing pairs.
instructions: Begin from a stretch position (like a pitcher with a runner on first). Emphasize on leg drive and finishing the throw to power the throw.
coaching_points: Use this to ramp arm strength up. Encourage players to feel the legs leading the throw.

name: Long Toss
setup: Players in pairs at a comfortable starting distance.
instructions: Begin playing catch with partners at a comfortable distance. After every couple throws, take one step back to build separation. Reach a maximum distance, then walk back in.
coaching_points: Reinforces the importance of distance and accuracy of throwing. Limit max distance to age-appropriate range.

name: Bucket Drill
setup: Place a bucket of balls behind the front foot of the hitter at the tee.
instructions: Hitter swings off the tee, attempting to brush the bucket with their front foot when they stride. This trains a controlled, short stride during the swing. Player digs balls out of the bucket during the drill.
coaching_points: Reinforces a soft front-side and prevents lunging.

name: Heavy Ball Drill
setup: Place a heavy ball on a tee.
instructions: Hitter takes a normal swing. The heavy ball trains a strong path through contact with the ball and forces the hitter to drive through the ball to the side of the heavier ball.
coaching_points: Helps build a confident, driving hand path. Don't let players over-swing.

name: Connection Ball Drill
equipment: Connection Ball (or rolled-up shirt/towel), Bats, Balls/Tee
setup: Place a connection ball or rolled-up shirt between both elbows of the hitter. The ball should hold in place as they get into their batting stance.
instructions: Hitter takes a swing without dropping the ball. The barrel of the bat should reach out around the barrel of the bat as they swing. Mounted on swinging through.
coaching_points: Forces the hitter to keep arms connected to the body through the swing; eliminates 'pulling off' the ball.

name: Block Drill
equipment: Block of wood (or 2x4), Tee, Bats, Balls
setup: Hitter starts in a normal batting stance.
instructions: Hitter takes a normal stance for a swing, with a block of wood (or 2x4) along the inside of their back foot. The block keeps the back foot from sliding forward and prevents the hitter from a back-foot hop. Hitter takes their swing keeping the back foot pinned to the block.
coaching_points: Trains weight transfer through the swing without leaking power off the back side.

name: Cage Work
equipment: Cage, Bat, Balls, L-Screen, Pitching Machine (optional)
setup: Setup a hitting cage with the hitter at a tee or live pitch from a coach behind an L-screen.
instructions: The batter practices identifying the pitch type and location as early as possible. The hitter is identifying the pitch and location, mimicking the sequence and timing of an at-bat. Especially helpful for tracking timing and pitch recognition.
coaching_points: Live reps; layer in pitch tracking, timing, and at-bat-style focus.

name: Backhand Drill
setup: Make a line of cones about 5 feet to the left of the players. Players line up at home plate.
instructions: Players line up at the cone closest to home plate. One at a time, in a hand toss to the backhand, the player stops the ball with their glove and uses two hands to bring the ball back to the chest. The player at the front of the line backhands and the next player rotates in.
coaching_points: Backhand technique: glove on the ground, two hands when possible, work feet to the ball.

name: Corners Drill
setup: Position 1 player at first, 1 at third base, and the remaining players line up behind them.
instructions: The player at 3B fields a hit and throws home, the throw goes out to first base for an out, the player goes to the back of the line. The player at 1B fields a hit and throws across the diamond to 3B (the throws of the line). The 3B players, the 1B players continue this pattern, the lines combine.
coaching_points: Trains fielding under pressure and accurate cross-diamond throws.

name: Footwork Drill
setup: Players line up at the cones (or position) at the dirt in front of them. Toss a ball to the side.
instructions: Players take 3 quick shuffle steps to get to the ball, field it, then make a quick controlled throw to a target. Run them through this from both backhand and forehand sides.
coaching_points: Quick feet, low base, gather and throw in rhythm.

name: Double Play Drill
setup: Split the players evenly between SS and 2B. Have a net or another coach at 1B to receive throws.
instructions: Coach hits ground balls between SS and 2B. The player at SS fields and tosses to 2B who turns and throws to 1B. The next player in line rotates to the position. Then have them switch which side starts the play.
coaching_points: Connect the two pieces — fielder + pivot. Glove flips on close balls, throws on stretchy ones.

name: Relay Drill
setup: Line three players in a long line about 30 feet apart. The closest player is the deep fielder.
instructions: The deep player throws the ball to the cut-off player. The cut-off catches and pivots, throwing to the third player. Run with one player at each spot, then rotate. Try to complete the relay in the fewest throws possible.
coaching_points: Hit the cut-off; pivot toward the throwing-side; receive on the glove side.

name: Scarecrow Drill
setup: Pitcher gets in a pitching stance with arms extended out like a scarecrow.
instructions: Lifting the front leg, slowly bring weight to the back leg. Slowly rotate to a pitching position with the front foot down and weight transferred. From this scarecrow, complete the pitching motion to the catcher.
coaching_points: Isolates balance and weight transfer at the slowest possible tempo.

name: Finish Drill
setup: Starting in an open position with the back foot in a pitcher's stance, glove and ball both at the chest.
instructions: Slowly rock the body forward and finish the pitch. The pitcher should be in a balanced position to finish the motion (head over feet, arm at the chest at the level of the throw).
coaching_points: Reinforces balanced finish and a controlled follow-through.

name: Towel Drill
setup: Players get into pitching stance with a towel in hand instead of a ball.
instructions: Place a glove or coach 1 target in front of the pitcher (about 1.5x stride length away). The pitcher's job is to throw the towel and hit the target. Focus on full extension out front.
coaching_points: Trains arm extension and finish without the stress of a ball.

name: Reach Back Drill
setup: Pitcher gets into the L position, arm bent at 90, glove side up. Front foot lands so the back foot is the back foot of the pitching motion.
instructions: After the player lifts his front foot, he must show the ball to the back fence (full reach back), then complete the throw. Repeat this on the same line as the catcher.
coaching_points: Promotes arm extension and a full throwing arc; reduces short-arming.

name: Knockout
setup: Set up a pyramid of cones (or cups) at the catcher's spot, behind home plate.
instructions: Players take turns throwing a pitch trying to knock down the most cones. Each pitch will count to score, the most cones at the end of the game wins. Keep rotating through the line.
coaching_points: Adds pressure and target-focus to bullpen reps.

name: Fly Ball Drill
setup: Set up 4 cones in a diamond pattern about 30 feet apart. Players line up at the cone on the right.
instructions: Throw a pop fly into the middle of the diamond. The first player runs under the ball to make the catch, then lines up at the next cone. Each player proceeds to catch a fly ball, starting from each cone.
coaching_points: Reads off the bat; get under the ball and use two hands.

name: On-The-Run Drill
setup: Players line up behind a cone next to the coach.
instructions: On the coach's signal, the first player starts to run. Coach throws a pop fly to the player who attempts to make the catch on the run. Player then runs the ball back to the coach and gets back in line. Each player takes a turn.
coaching_points: Trains running catches and tracking on the move.

name: Blind Fly Ball Drill
setup: 3-4 players line up side-by-side, 10 feet apart, in the outfield facing the fence.
instructions: Coach hits a fly ball toward the players. When players hear the ball hit the bat, they turn around, find the ball, and attempt to catch it in the air. The player closest to the ball calls 'I got it!' and makes the catch. Other players back off once the ball is called.
coaching_points: Trains reaction, communication, and calling for the ball.

name: Outfield Footwork Drill
setup: Players start in the outfield 8-10 feet apart, facing the coach.
instructions: Players respond to the coach's signals: Point right = left foot crossover then sprint right 3 steps. Point left = right foot crossover then sprint left 3 steps. Point back right = right foot drop step then sprint back right 3 steps. Point back left = left foot drop step then sprint back left 3 steps.
coaching_points: Drop step, crossover step, then turn-and-go. Quality over speed.

name: Target Drill
setup: Players line up in center field. Three buckets are stacked in a triangle on home plate.
instructions: Players take turns throwing a ball from center field to home plate. The first player to knock over the buckets wins.
coaching_points: Hit the cut-off in real games; here, focus on long-throw accuracy and arm strength.

name: Rounding 1st Base Drill
setup: Players line up at home plate. Place a cone outside the 1B line and a 2nd cone 10 ft from 1B.
instructions: Player 1 runs from home to first, taking a wide angle outside of the first cone to make the turn, stepping on the inside corner of 1B with his right foot. Player continues on to second base staying inside of the second cone. Next player continues until everyone has gone.
coaching_points: Banana the path; right foot on the inside corner; head up to look for the ball.

name: Sliding Drill
setup: Players line up behind a cone. About 40 feet from the cone, place a few sheets of cardboard.
instructions: One at a time, each player takes a turn running and sliding onto the cardboard. Practice proper feet-first sliding technique: lead leg extended, trailing leg folded at a right angle under the lead leg.
coaching_points: Hands up, slide on the bottom (not the side), eyes forward.

name: Tag Up Drill
setup: Start with runners on all 3 bases. The rest of the players line up at home plate.
instructions: Coach stands in middle of infield and tosses himself a high fly ball. Player at home plate runs to 1B. The other three runners tag up on their base and prepare to advance once the coach catches the ball. Don't leave early!
coaching_points: Eyes on the catch, not the ball — wait for first contact.

name: Reaction Drill
setup: Players line up at first base.
instructions: One at a time, they take the position of a runner on first base. Coach throws a ball up in the air. Runner cannot leave the base until the ball hits the ground. As soon as it hits, runner takes off toward 2B. This works on the runner's reaction time.
coaching_points: Explosive first step; head down in the first three steps.

name: Base Race Drill
setup: Players line up at home plate.
instructions: On the coach's signal the first player begins to run the bases. Time each player as they run from home all the way around. Alternatively, have the next runner start running once the runner in front reaches 1B. Don't let the runner behind you pass you!
coaching_points: Tighten the angles around 1B and 2B; head up; full speed home.

name: Wild Pitch Drill
setup: Catcher gets in stance behind home plate. Coach stands in front of home plate.
instructions: Coach throws a ball against the backstop. Catcher pops up, turns around, locates the ball, and gets to it as fast as possible. Catcher then makes a good throw to coach at home plate.
coaching_points: Find the ball first, then get to it; controlled throw, not a panic throw.

name: Blocking Drill
setup: Catcher starts in stance behind home plate.
instructions: Coach throws a pitch that lands in the dirt in front of the catcher. Catcher drops to his knees with legs wide, throwing hand behind glove covering the hole between legs. Chin is down. Catcher uses his body to block the ball, attempting to have it bounce back onto home plate.
coaching_points: Chin down, glove between knees, soft chest, ball bounces in front of you.

name: Stance Drill
setup: Start in an athletic stance, feet shoulder-width apart.
instructions: Drop your elbows to your knees, keeping your back flat. With toes pointed slightly to the outside, shift weight back and forth. Slowly sit back, lowering your body as you continue to shift until you reach a comfortable squatting position.
coaching_points: Comfortable squat, back flat, weight balanced. Build endurance for game-like reps.

name: Catcher Pop Up Drill
setup: Catcher starts in stance behind home plate.
instructions: Coach says 'go' and throws a ball straight up in the air behind the catcher. Catcher pops up, removes mask, and finds the ball. Once the catcher locates the ball, he tosses the mask in the other direction and attempts to catch the ball. Make sure not to toss the mask until you have located the ball.
coaching_points: Find ball first, then toss mask away from where you'll catch.

name: Throw Down Drill
setup: Catcher gets in stance behind home plate. A player is in position at SS / 2B as a tag receiver.
instructions: Coach throws a pitch to the catcher. The catcher receives, transfers, and makes a throw to the SS/2B as if a runner is stealing. Repeat to build accuracy and quickness.
coaching_points: Footwork (jab step), clean transfer, low throw to the bag.

name: Plastic Ball Tag
instructions:
• The first round of this freeze-tag style game is playing in an open field.
• The second round is played only using fair territory of the field.
• In the third round, when the players are tagged they not only freeze, but they freeze in the
position of a batter.

name: Grip And Throw
instructions:
• While players are circled around the coach, the correct grip is shown and each player
practices holding the ball.

name: Run The Bases
instructions:
• Following the coach, the players run/jog around the bases while calling out each base that
they touch.
• For round two, the players will advance to each base one at a time and will stop on each
base. They will move to the next base when they are cued.
• An option is to have a coach with a ball in his or her hand ready to tag players who come off
of the base.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 17

name: Statues
instructions:
• Players stay in the infield and freeze like a statue when instructed by the coach.
• In the second round, the coach tags the players to freeze instead of just calling out “freeze.”

name: Team Throwing
equipment: Plastic Balls | Fence | Hula Hoops | Cones | String
instructions:
• Players are grouped into teams. On “go” the first player from each team begins by trying to
throw their ball through or into the hoop. As each player gets the ball through the hoop, his
or her team counts the outs.

name: Practice Swing
instructions:
• While players are taking dry swings, the coach calls one player at a time over to the tee
for practice.

name: Left Field, Center Field, Right Field
instructions:
• The players begin in left field. When the coach calls out another outfield position, the players
run to the cone in that specific position.
• Once game begins, the coach can call out a position at any time, even if the players are
running between positions.

name: Position Fitness
instructions:
• The players and coach begin at home plate. The coach announces the position, and
then he or she demonstrates an exercise for the players to complete. Players and coach
complete repetitions of the exercise together before moving on to the next position
and exercise.

• Players then stand up and practice dry swings.

name: Swing Review
instructions:
• Players sit in grass while coach reviews swing and swinging safety rules.
• Players then stand up and practice dry swings.

name: Swing And Run
equipment: Bat | Bases | Helmets | Optional Equipment: Tee and Tee Balls
instructions:
• The game is played just like the activity “Base Running,” but now a practice swing is added
before the players run.
OPTION: Have a tee set with a ball and have the players hit the ball before running instead of just taking a
practice swing.
• Players advance one base at a time, and are moved to the next base by the next player.
OPTION: A coach has a ball in his/her hand and tags runners who come off of the bases at the wrong times.

PRACTICE THROWING

Tee Balls
DRILL SEQUENCE:
• The players play catch with a partner.
• Practice fielding a ground ball can be incorporated into this activity by players taking turns
rolling the ball to each other and throwing it back.

name: Practice Throwing
instructions:
• The players play catch with a partner.
• Practice fielding a ground ball can be incorporated into this activity by players taking turns
rolling the ball to each other and throwing it back.

name: Clean Up The Backyard
equipment: Tennis Balls or Plastic Balls | Cones
instructions:
• The players are divided into two teams. Each team is responsible for one side of the playing
area that is divided by cones.
• All types of soft or squishy balls (tennis or plastic balls) are scattered on both sides of the
playing area.
• On “go,” players are to throw or toss the balls on their team’s side to the other team’s side
continually until time is called.
• The team with the least numbers of balls on their side when time is called wins.

name: Fielding
instructions:
• In separate lines the players line up and receive a ground ball from a coach.
• The player fields the ground ball rolled to him/her and throws it back to the coach before
returning to the end of their line.

name: Fielding In Positions
instructions:
• Each position should be marked with cones before the drill starts. The players are sent
to positions.
• Before the drill begins, review fielding a ground ball with the players once they are in positions.
• The coach at home plate rolls the ball to the players in position, one at a time. The player who
fields the ball then throws it back to the coach on the pitcher’s plate.

name: Fielding With A Runner (Optional Drill)
instructions:
• Players are in position on the field with any extra players in a small line by the coach at
home plate.
• On “go” the coach rolls a ball from home plate to a position and the runner at home plate
runs to first base at the same time.
• The fielder must field the ball and throw it to the pitcher before the runner gets to first base.
If the runner “beats the play” they stay at first base and if the runner does not “beat the
play” they go back to the end of the line at home plate.

Bases
FIRST!
DRILL SEQUENCE:
• Starting at home plate, everyone jogs to first, second, third, and home in a line, following the
coach and calling out the bases as they go.
• On round 2, start the line at home plate, on “go” the first player runs to first and stays on first.
On the next “go”, the player on first advances to second and the new runner goes to first.
Repeat with all players running and all advancing until each player scores at home plate.
• Optional to have a coach on the field with a ball in hand, stressing that the base means SAFE
and if they are off the base they could be tagged OUT.

name: Tee Hitting
instructions:
• The players are split into groups and take turns hitting off a tee into a net, fence, or open
field with a coach.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 39

name: Red Light, Green Light
instructions:
• All players line up on the foul line in the outfield and the coaches face the players a distance
away. When a coach calls out “green light,” the players begin running toward the coach. When
the coach calls out “red light,” the players must stop or freeze.
• The coach continues to call out green and red light until players reach a determined distance.

name: Catching Practice
instructions:
• The players find a personal space anywhere in the playing area. The players should all have
his/her glove and tennis ball.
• Players toss the ball in the air to themselves and catch it, or “squeeze it,” in their gloves.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 43
 SEQUENCE 4                                                                                • ONLINE VIDEO
OFFENSE AND DEFENSE - PROGRESSION 1 & 2
WHAT YOU’LL NEED:
Tee Balls | Bases | Buckets (3)
LITTLE LEAGUE ®
DRILL SEQUENCE:
• The players begin the drill in positions. The coach rolls the ball to any position. The player at
the specific position must field the ball and then either run it or throw it to a designated player
(usually the person playing first base). That player then drops the ball into the bucket beside
him/her and it counts as an “out.”
• PROGRESSION 2: The player who fields the ball must throw the ball (and not run it) to the
designated player with the bucket for an out.

name: Offense And Defense - Progression 3
equipment: Tee Balls | Bases | Buckets (3) | Bats | Helmets | Tees
instructions:
• The players are divided into two teams. One team must go behind the line of cones in the
field, and the other team is near home plate with a tee and plastic balls (or in line at a tee
ready to take a turn).
• On “go”, the players at the tees all swing and hit their plastic balls into the field. The players
in the field stay behind the cone line to field the balls and then run to place them in the
bucket that is also behind the cone line in the field.
• The game is continuous and teams should switch sides after a specific time or until all of the
balls are gone. All players (or most) are moving at all times.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 45

name: Zigzagging
instructions:
• The players are broken up into groups. Each group lines up behind a line of spaced
out cones.
• On “go”, the first player in each line zigzags through the cones, circles around the last
cones, and zigzags back between the cones. They then tag the next person in line to
proceed through the cones.
• Finish when all players are complete or turn the drill into a race between teams.

name: Pop-Ups
instructions:
• The players are split up into groups and paired with a coach.
• Each group circles around or spreads out around the coach. The coach takes turn with each
player and tosses him/her a very shallow pop-up, progressing higher and higher with
each turn.
• After a few practice rounds, each group has a contest within itself to see which player can
catch the most pop ups in a row. However many each player catches within each group, the
other group members do that many jumping jacks before the next player’s turn.

name: Run The Bases Relay
instructions:
• The players are divided into two teams. One team lines up at second base and the other
team lines up at home plate. Each line should be out of the way of the base paths.
• On “go”, the first player in line at second base runs around the bases and back to second
base while, at the same time, the player at home runs around the bases back to home plate.
Once the players arrive back to their team’s line they tag the next player to continue
the race.
• The first team to finish is the winning team.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 51

name: The Great Baseball
instructions:
• Break the players into four groups. Each group should be sent to a base running line. Give
each group a nickname such as, “The Baseballs,” or “The Bats.”
• A coach stands in the middle of the field and calls out a team’s nickname. When that team
is called, the team must run to the other side (opposite of them) without being tagged by the
coach.
• If players get tagged on their way to the other side, they must sit down in the playing area
and become a stationary tagger while other groups are called to cross.

name: Hit The Bucket
instructions:
• All players make a large circle around a bucket. Each player takes a turn and tosses a
plastic ball that they have a the bucket, trying to get the ball inside the bucket.
• If a player hits the bucket with their ball, it counts as an out for the team. If a player gets
their ball inside the bucket, it counts as three outs for the team and the round in over. The
team is trying to get three outs.
• The drill may progress to see how many balls the team can toss inside the bucket during a
specified time period.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 55

name: Follow The Leader
instructions:
• All players line up on the first base line behind a coach.
• The coach moves different ways, such as skipping, running, hopping, jumping, and
zigzagging, all around the field while the players follow behind mimicking the
coach’s movements.

name: Copycat (Modification to Sequence 2)
instructions:
• The players find a personal space in the playing area with the coach facing the players.
• The coach stays in a stationary spot, while doing several different movements and the
players must copy the movements.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 59

• Station 1: Practice Throwing – Players practice throwing with a partner. Then the players all

• Station 2: Practice Swings – Players practice swinging with a bat. Then players take turns

• The groups switch after a specific time.

name: Beach Volleyball Circle
instructions:
• The players remain in groups from the last activity (or break them into groups).
• Each group creates a circle with a coach.
• The coach begins bumping a beach volleyball into the air. The players try to keep the
volleyball in the air by calling the ball and hitting it in the air within the circle.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 61

name: Races
instructions:
• Separate the players into two groups. Each group is in a line behind the foul line and the
coach stands across from the groups.
• On “go” the first player from each group races past the imaginary line past the coach. The
next person in each line races on “go” and so on.

name: Show And Tell
equipment: Equipment for each player’s chosen skill
instructions:
• The players are in a small cluster or circle sitting on the grass.
• Each player has a chance to come in front of the group and show a skill that they think they
are awesome at completing or really good at doing, like throwing, fielding, running, and more.

• The players practice running around the base, calling out the bases as they go around on
the coach’s cues.

name: Station 2
instructions:
• The players are staggered into mock positions, but not as far apart as actual outfielders.
• The coach tosses pop-ups or ground balls to each player. The players practice calling the
ball when it comes to them.
The Little League® Tee Ball Program | 67

name: Inning Practice
equipment: Tee Balls | Bases | Bats | Helmets | Gloves
setup: Divide the players in half: half on offense, half playing field positions on defense.
instructions: Work through a mini-inning of game-like play. The defense practices fielding live tee'd hits. Each offensive player gets to hit off the tee and run the bases. Switch sides after every player has had a turn batting.
coaching_points: Reinforce running through 1B, calling for the ball, and listening for coaches' instructions.

name: Two-and-Three Finger Grips
setup: Players in three single-file lines of four, one coach per line.
instructions: Players grab a ball off the ground and show you their four-seam grip. Each player does five balls. Demonstrate proper four-seam grip. Show two-finger and three-finger grips: index finger on top of the ball, thumb on the bottom, middle finger on top. Spacing between fingers about the size of a finger. Players grip the ball across the horseshoe ('C').
coaching_points: Quick reset between balls. Make every grip a four-seam.

name: Four-Seam Relay Race
setup: Three lines of four players, about 15 feet from a coach. One ball on the ground in front of each line.
instructions: Player starts from their line, runs up to the ball, picks it up, and shows the coach their four-seam grip. Returns to the back of their line. Once they return, the next player goes. Continue until everyone has gone. The relay is run after the drill.
coaching_points: Quality of the grip > speed. Pause to fix bad grips.

name: Toss/Catch/Four-Seam Grip
instructions:
Each player will start with a ball. The player will throw the ball in
the air, work on catching with two hands above the waist.
Once the ball is caught, the player will grip the ball with a
four-seam grip and transition in to the “launch” position of throwing.

20 tosses each.

1.3

name: Toss/Catch/Four-Seam Grip Relay
setup: Four teams of three players each, in a straight line about 10 feet apart.
instructions: Once the first player completes the toss/catch/four-seam grip drill, the next player goes. Relay is the first team to complete two or three successful rounds.
coaching_points: Reinforce the four-seam grip transition every rep — speed without sloppy grips.

name: Player Toss
setup: Players partnered with someone of similar ability, about 10-15 feet apart.
instructions: Partner tosses the ball; receiver catches with two hands and transitions into a four-seam grip. Once the thrower shows a Two-Hand Target (2HT), the receiver tosses the ball back. Continue for 15 throws each.
coaching_points: 2HT before every throw; clean transition glove → throwing hand → grip.

name: Two-Hand Target (2HT)
setup: Pairs of players facing each other.
instructions: When playing catch, the thrower should not deliver the ball until the receiver shows a 2HT. The 2HT is when the receiver has both arms extended straight out from the body with a slight elbow flex, hands straight up, thumbs toward each other. Once the thrower sees the 2HT they may deliver the ball.
coaching_points: No throw without a target. Receiver builds the habit of presenting hands first.

name: Thumb-to-Thumb (T2T)
setup: Pairs of players facing each other.
instructions: When receiving the ball above the waist, the receiver shows a 2HT and catches the ball thumb-to-thumb. Emphasizes using two hands and allows the receiver to quickly transition from glove to throwing hand using the four-seam grip.
coaching_points: Above the waist → thumbs together. Always two hands.

name: Pinky-to-Pinky
setup: Pairs of players facing each other.
instructions: When receiving the ball below the waist, the receiver shows a 2HT and catches the ball pinky-to-pinky. Stresses two-hand catching and proper technique below the waist.
coaching_points: Below the waist → pinkies together. Always two hands.

name: Below Waist Catching
setup: Players in three single-file lines of four. One coach per line.
instructions: The coach throws the ball below the waist to each player to work on the pinky-to-pinky two-hand technique. 15-20 throws per player, rotating after each throw.
coaching_points: Watch the ball into the hands; pinkies together every catch.

name: Above Waist Catching
setup: Players in three single-file lines of four. One coach per line.
instructions: Coach reviews pinky-to-pinky catching, then throws the ball above the waist for each player to work on the thumb-to-thumb, two-hand technique. 15-20 throws per player, rotating after each throw.
coaching_points: Above the waist → thumbs together. Both hands move to the ball.

name: Plastic Ball Pop Ups
setup: Three single-file lines of four players, one coach per line.
instructions: Coach throws plastic balls to a designated area in the air. Players line up underneath the ball and try to make the catch with two hands — T2T if the ball is above the waist, P2P if below. 10-15 throws per player.
coaching_points: Get under the ball first, then square up. Two hands every time.

name: Knock Out Game
setup: Split each team into four players. Teams line up behind first, second, and third bases. Coach on pitcher's mound.
instructions: When their team is called, the first player receives a pop-up thrown from the coach. After a successful catch, the player goes to the end of the line. Once a player misses, they sit at the end of their line and cheer for their team. Game finishes when there is one player left.
coaching_points: Pressure reps; encourage teammates between catches.

name: Tennis Ball Pop Ups
setup: Three single-file lines of four players, one coach per line.
instructions: Coach throws fly balls with tennis balls. Players react, line up underneath the ball, and try to catch with two hands using T2T (above the waist) or P2P (below the waist). The throwing hand secures the ball, transitioning to a four-seam grip. 10-15 throws per player.
coaching_points: Tennis balls are forgiving — emphasize technique over fear of getting hit.

name: Drop Step and Crossover
setup: Three single-file lines of four players, one coach per line.
instructions: Coach throws a tennis ball in one of four directions. Ball out to the right: cross right foot over left and run toward the ball. Ball right and back: drop step with the left foot, run back at an angle, look over right shoulder. Ball out to the left: cross left foot over right and run toward the ball. Ball left and back: drop step with right foot, run back at an angle, look over left shoulder. Players square up under the ball and catch with two hands using T2T. 10 throws per player.
coaching_points: Drop step before crossover; never backpedal. Eyes on the ball.

name: Five Steps of Throwing
instructions:
Step One: Step
Start square to your partner, step towards your partner with the foot of your throwing hand. Plant your foot with the
inside of the foot facing the receiver, this will align the glove shoulder to your partner.
Step Two: Shoulder-to-Partner
You will want to have your glove shoulder facing your partner. The thrower’s hands are to move downward towards
the center of their body until they separate. This will lead you to the launch, which is the next step.
Step Three: Launch
At this point the thrower will turn their thumbs in to get the elbows up putting the arms in the launch position. The
ball will be in the throwing hand away from the receiver with a four-seam grip and the knuckles of the throwing hand
facing the receiver.
Step Four: Delivery
The thrower should stay behind the ball when throwing and snap their wrist when throwing to the receiver.
Step Five: Finish
The thrower’s weight will continue towards the receiver and the arm will follow through to the 2HT.

Start in the “launch” position, focus on the 2HT using a four-seam grip. Continue Drill for 15-20 throws.

name: Hula Hoop Game
setup: Three single-file lines of four players. Hula hoop on the fence/backstop.
instructions: Players see how many of five throws they can put through the hula hoop. Use the four-seam grip and full Five Steps of Throwing.
coaching_points: Targets sharpen accuracy. Step direct at the hoop, finish to the target.

name: Throwing from the Knee to Partner
setup: Partners of like ability, 15 feet apart. Each takes a knee — glove-hand knee raised, throwing-hand knee on the ground.
instructions: Players throw to each other from the knee. The directional shoulder is pointed at the 2HT. Reinforces delivery step of throwing and works on T2T catching. 15-20 throws each.
coaching_points: Knee down on throwing side; eyes on the 2HT; clean wrist snap.

name: Hand Separation
instructions:
Partner players with similar abilities. Have each player stand 15 to 20 feet apart. Each player will have his/her
directional side toward the partner to start the drill. Hands together on the center of the body (chest) with ball
pressed into glove with throwing hand. Elbows are down. The throwing hand and glove hand, move down the
center of the together and separate with the thumbs turning in toward the body, moving the elbows up. This will put
the thrower in the launch position: 20 to 25 throws, increasing distance after 10 and 20 throws.

name: Game of 21
instructions:
Match players of like ability for this game. To start the drill, play to
11, until the players are skilled enough to play to 21.

name: Three-Man Relay
instructions:
Three-Man Relay
This drill simulates the correct technique for completing a throw
from the outfield, to a relay man, to the base. Emphasize correct
throwing technique and to teach the skill of relaying the ball in this
sequence.

Players should be in a straight line approximately 25–55 feet
apart. Coaches will adjust the distance for the players. The drill
begins with a ball on the ground in the outfield. The outfielder will
pick the ball up and make a good throw using proper throwing
mechanics to the relay man. The relay man will stand sideways
with their directional shoulder (glove hand) pointed toward the
target they will be relaying the ball to, in this case the base. The
third man will quickly return the throw back to the relay man who
will make the final throw to the outfielder. Place the ball on the
ground and repeat.

Complete drill 15 times.

instructions:
Long Toss

moving a step further away from their partner after each throw,

name: Grip / Stance / Coverage
setup: Players spread out with bats.
instructions: GRIP: Place both hands flat and lay the bat at the base of the fingers. Lightly wrap fingers around the bat. Knuckles should align (straight or slightly shifted). STANCE: Athletic position, knees slightly bent, feet shoulder-width apart. Weight 40% front foot / 60% back foot. COVERAGE: Get into stance and place the bat at the corner of the plate closest to the catcher — the bat must cover the whole plate so the hitter can drive the outside pitch.
coaching_points: Re-check grip → stance → coverage every at-bat. Habits compound.

name: Dry Swings
instructions:
Each coach will have four players in their group. Players will be
about 10 to 12 feet away from each other. They will place their
fielding glove on the ground and use it as home plate. The coach
will have each player take a swing on their command and work
3.2
with them to correct their swing.
Each player will properly grip the bat, get into a good stance and
make sure to cover the plate. A coach will throw off of one knee
from about 35 feet away from the plate. (The use of a protective “L”
screen is highly recommended.) The coach will throw five pitches
to each player. Split the team into three groups of four players.
The other three players will be outside the fence waiting to hit.
Once all players on Group A have hit then Group B who was in the
infield will hit and Group C who was in the outfield will move into
the infield. Group A will move out to the outfield. Rotate through
until all groups have had a chance to hit, play the infield, and play
the outfield.
3.3

2015 Little League Baseball® Coach Pitch 		 Week One | Page 11

name: Coach Pitching from Knee
setup: Coach pitches from one knee, ~35 feet from the plate, behind an L-screen.
instructions: Each player grips the bat properly, gets into a good stance, and covers the plate. Coach throws five pitches per player. Split team into three groups of four — Group A hits, B in the infield, C in the outfield. After Group A finishes, B hits and C moves to the infield, A moves to the outfield. Rotate through.
coaching_points: L-screen is mandatory. Pitch off the knee — players see the ball clearly.

name: Hitting from a Tee
setup: Three groups (A/B/C). Tees set up at netted/fenced areas.
instructions: Each player hits five balls off the tee into a net or fence while waiting to hit live from the coach. Repeat three times.
coaching_points: Tee work is technique work — slow them down on bad reps.

name: Pitch Recognition
setup: Coach acts as the pitcher; hitter is in the box wearing a helmet.
instructions: Coach fakes a pitching motion but holds up a number of fingers as he releases. The player must call out the number of fingers as soon as they see them.
coaching_points: Trains tracking the release point. Eyes locked on the coach's hand.

name: Game: Conditioning
instructions:
Split the group into two teams. The first team hits while the other is in the field. A coach pitches (protected by an
“L” screen). The first batter hits the ball and starts to run the bases. The team in the field all run to the ball and line
up behind it. They pass the ball through the legs of each player until the last player at the end of the line gets it
and throws it to the coach who is pitching. When the ball gets to the coach, the runner stops. Each base touched
counts as one point for the team. Immediately the next hitter gets a pitch and the same thing happens. Once every
player hits once, the total bases for the team are added up for their score. They take the field, and the other team
comes in to hit and tries to beat their score. This game is more fun with live hitting and hustling around the bases
mixed in.

name: Soft Toss
instructions:
Each player will hit nine balls. Players will hit three, then rotate for
three sets. This will keep the players engaged. A coach will crouch
down on the opposite side of the hitter’s stance.
Each player will do this drill three times. Each coach will have
four hitters. One set of hitters will be at home hitting towards the
outfield. The second set of hitters will be at the right field foul pole
hitting towards second base. The third set of hitters will be on the
left field foul pole hitting towards second base.
Players not hitting will be waiting for their turn away from the hitter
and hitter’s path. Make sure that each player is approaching
their at-bats as if it were in a game. Players must be wearing
batting helmets.

instructions:
Coach Pitch 4x4x4
This drill/game will focus on the coach pitching to the players.
Each player will approach their at-bat as if it is in a game and
make sure they have proper coverage of the plate. There will be
three groups of four. Group One will be batting, Group Two will

name: Coach Pitch 6x6
instructions:
Coach Pitch 6x6		
This game will be similar to a regular baseball game, playing four
innings. Coach will pitch to the players from a knee or standing
from 40 feet away. Each player will approach their at-bat as if it is
in a game and make sure they have proper coverage of the plate.
There will be two groups of six players each. Group One will be
batting, Group Two will be infielders and outfielders. The three
players who are outfielders in the first inning will be infielders the
next inning. Keep this rotation for the remainder of the game. Each
team will get an inning to hit (three outs) and will play the game
as if it is a live game. The fielders will try and get each hitter out.
Once Group One has three outs or five runs scored the inning will
end and Group Two will come in to hit and Group One will play the
field. This rotation will continue until the game is over.

name: Purpose of Base Running
setup: Players gathered on the infield grass.
instructions: Explain that the goal is to score more runs than the other team. To score, a runner must travel home → 1B → 2B → 3B → home. The team with more runs wins. It doesn't matter how you get on base — walk, hit, or error — once you're on base you can score.
coaching_points: Plain language; check for understanding by asking 'how do we score?'

name: Run Through First Base
instructions:
Form four lines of players, with three in each line. Explain that on
a ball hit in the infield you want to run as fast as you can through
first base. Do not slow down in front of the base. This drill will help
eliminate running and stopping on the base.
Use home plate to first base as line one. Create line two, three, and
four using the same distance beside line one. If you have throw
down bases use them, if not use a fielding glove or something
similar.
A player will run through first base hitting the front of the base with
either foot. Once the player runs through the base the player will
chop their feet to stop, while looking to the right to see if the ball
was overthrown. Do this drill five times each.

name: Merry-Go-Round
instructions:
This is a fun drill that will allow the players to run the bases and get
an understanding of how to run base to base. Start with an even
number of players at each base, including home plate. One player
will approach the plate with a bat with one player on each base.

They will get a proper grip on the bat. They will get in their stance
and check to see their plate coverage. Once the coach says “go,”
the player will swing the bat like they just hit the ball and will run
toward first base. This will set the drill in motion. The player on first
base will run to second base.

The player at second base will run to third base. The player on
third bases will run to home plate. Each player will go to the end
of the line at the next base. Continue this drill until each player has
“hit” two-to-three times.

name: Rounding First Base
instructions:
Players will get into one line on the grass beside home plate toward the third base dugout. Players will go up to the
plate with a bat, get into their stance, and make sure they cover the plate. Players will swing as if they are hitting
the ball, they will drop the bat after two steps to the right, along the first base line. They will run about 45 feet in a
straight line towards first.
Once they are about 10 to 15 feet before first base the runner will bow out to the right making their path from home
look like similar to a question mark (?) once they round first base. This will allow the runner to round first base and
start to head towards second base. For this drill the runner will go about 10 to 15 feet beyond first base looking
toward the outfielder who fielded the ball and return to first base. Do this drill five times each.

2015 Little League Baseball® Coach Pitch 		 Week Three | Page 26

name: Home Plate Relay Race
instructions:
Review Pinky-to-Pinky catching. Coaches will have the players
line up into three single file lines of four players each. One coach
per line will throw each player 10 balls.
The coach will throw the ball to players above the waist, to work
on thumb to thumb, two hand technique. Players will line up in
three single file lines of four players each. One coach per line
15-20 throws per player, rotate after each throw.
GAME:
Award the player a point for each ball caught. Team with the most
points wins.

THROWING REVIEW
–– Do not throw until you see a Two-Hand Target (2HT)
–– Use a four-seam grip.
–– FIVE STEPS OF THROWING
Step One: Step
Start square to your partner, step towards your partner with the foot of your throwing hand. Plant your foot with
the inside of the foot facing the receiver, this will align the glove shoulder to your partner. (Fig. 2.1)
Step Two: Shoulder-to-Partner
You will want to have your glove shoulder facing your partner. The thrower’s hands are to move downward
towards the center of their body until they separate. This will lead you to the launch, which is the next step.
(Fig. 2.2)
Step Three: Launch
At this point the thrower will turn their thumbs in to get the elbows up putting the arms in the launch position. The ball
will be in the throwing hand away from the receiver with a four-seam grip and the knuckles of the throwing hand facing
the receiver. (Fig. 2.3)
Step Four: Delivery
[truncated]

name: Base Running Cues
instructions:
Players are to start at home and determine how they will approach
first base by the cues given to them by the first-base coach. If
the coach points to the base and says “base” the player will run
through first base. If the coach points at second base and tells
them “turn“ the batter/runner will begin to curve out to the right
about 10-15 feet before first base. The runner will bow out the right
making their path from home look similar to a question mark (?)
once they touch first base. This will allow the runner to touch first
base and start to head to second base in a straight line. For this
drill the runner will go about 10-15 feet beyond the base looking
towards the outfielder who fielded the ball. This gives the base
runner cues on how to approach first base, advance or turn back
and run quickly to first base.

HOME PLATE RELAY RACE
GAME: HOME PLATE RELAY RACE

name: First-to-Third
setup: Runner at first base; coach acts as the third base coach.
instructions: Runner runs as fast as they can toward second base. About 10-12 feet from second, they turn their head toward the third base coach to get the signal — advance to third or stay at second.
coaching_points: Run hard until the signal — don't peek early. Pick up the coach.

name: Second-to-Home
instructions:
Second-To-Home
Introduce running from second-to-home. Players will curve out
when approaching third base, this is done to allow the runner to
hit the inside of the base and be in as close of a straight line while
advancing towards home.

FIRST-TO-THIRD                    First-to-Third
First-to-third is the other base running drill. Runners will run as fast
as they can toward second base. When the runner is about 10 to
12 feet from second base, the runner will turn his/her head toward
the third base coach and get the signal of advancing to third base
or staying at second base.

LOOK FOR
COACH’S SIGNAL

2015 Little League Baseball® Coach Pitch 		Week Seven | Page 56

name: Home-to-First; First-to-Third; Second-to-Home
setup: Players line up at home plate; coach signals at third.
instructions: Combine the three base-running progressions. (1) Home-to-first: run through the bag. (2) First-to-third: run hard, look for third base coach's signal at ~12 feet from second. (3) Second-to-home: curve out approaching third, hit the inside of the bag, straight line for home. Walk through each, then run live.
coaching_points: Inside corners on the turns; head up looking for the next base.

name: Five Steps of Fielding
instructions:
–– Step One: Creeper Steps
Player will take two steps towards the hitter. First step is with the throwing hand, second step is with the glove hand.
The glove foot will be slightly out front of the throwing foot. (Fig. 4.1 Pg. 7)
–– Step Two: Bend Knees / Lower Torso Down
Player will have knees bent and will have their body lowered down so that their glove is touching the ground in a
“ready” position. Imagine sitting down on a chair; now come off of that chair where you are barely standing above it.
This will be the position that you need to be in. (Fig. 4.2 Pg. 7)
–– Step Three: Glove Out Front
Player will be in ready position with their arms extended out in front of their body. The palm of the glove will be facing
the hitter and low to the ground. The throwing hand should be above the glove forming the mouth of an alligator.
(Fig. 4.3 Pg. 7)
–– Step Four: Receive / Suck / Funnel / Move
Players will field the ball out in front of their body with “alligator hands” and bring the ball into their mid-section. At this
time the player will use the throwing hand of the alligator hands to grip the ball in a four seam grip. At the same time
the player should move their body, throwing foot then glove foot towards the direction where the throw will be made.
When finished with this step, the shoulder of the glove hand should be pointed at the target. (Fig. 4.4 Pg. 7)
–– Step Five: Throw to Target
